handbook.warbands.1.title: Warbands
handbook.warbands.1.body:
Found a town, gather resources and train soldiers who follow you into battle.

This is a mid-game adventure: you will need diamonds, emeralds and gold.

Turn pages with the arrows below.
handbook.warbands.2.title: The Path
handbook.warbands.2.body:
1. Craft a Town Center Blueprint and build it.
2. Stock food, wood, stone and gold.
3. Train soldiers and lead them with a War Horn.
4. Build houses to grow your army.
5. Take enemy camps with War Maps: their trophies unlock the next age.
6. Advance to unlock new buildings.

This guide follows the same order.
handbook.warbands.3.title: Town Center
handbook.warbands.3.body:
The blueprint recipe is above. Emeralds come from villagers.

Right-click the core block to open it: deposit resources, train soldiers, advance ages.

Only you can break the core, while sneaking, and that ends your town. Keep 128 blocks between your Town Centers.
handbook.warbands.4.title: Building
handbook.warbands.4.body:
Hold a blueprint to see the outline where you look.

Green: it fits. Red: something is in the way.
White: the entrance. Click the block in front of it.

Natural terrain (dirt, stone, plants) is cleared for you.
handbook.warbands.5.title: Stockpile
handbook.warbands.5.body:
Open the Town Center and put items in Deposit. They turn into resources:

Food: any food, by hunger value
Wood: log 4, plank 1
Stone: 1 per block (for ages and buildings)
Gold: nugget 1, ingot 9, block 81
handbook.warbands.6.title: Units
handbook.warbands.6.body:
Train them at the Town Center. Cost and time are shown on the buttons.

Militia: sword and shield, fights up close.
Archer: shoots from range.

Queue up to 5. New soldiers wait outside the building until you come near or blow the horn. Each soldier takes 1 population; houses raise the limit.
handbook.warbands.7.title: Your Army
handbook.warbands.7.body:
Soldiers follow you, attack what you attack and defend you. Left 24+ blocks behind, they teleport to you. They step aside when you walk into them.

Feed them to heal. Death is permanent.

A War Horn gives them orders.
handbook.warbands.8.title: Houses
handbook.warbands.8.body:
Recipe above. Build it near your Town Center (30 stone).

Population: 5, plus 5 per house, up to 50 (more in later ages).

A house counts while its hearth stands and at least half its blocks remain.
handbook.warbands.9.title: Rules
handbook.warbands.9.body:
Buildings are one piece: their blocks drop nothing, even from explosions, and pistons can't move them.

Only you can open your Town Center. Its core block breaks only while you sneak, and breaking it loses the stockpile, age and queue.

Your soldiers never hurt you, your pets or each other.

handbook.warbands.10.title: Ages
handbook.warbands.10.body:
Put the trophy in the Town Center's Deposit and press Advance.

Feudal: 500 food, 200 stone, 200 gold, a Bandit Trophy, 60 s.
Castle: 800 food, 400 stone, 500 gold, a Fort Trophy, 90 s.

Trophies come from taking camps (see War Maps). The Town Center is rebuilt and your whole army gets stronger.
handbook.warbands.12.title: Castle Age
handbook.warbands.12.body:
For every soldier you have, and every new one. Militia and Spearmen get diamond weapons.

New: Stable, Watch Tower, Siege Workshop, and Castle upgrades at the Blacksmith.
handbook.warbands.11.title: Feudal Age
handbook.warbands.11.body:
For every soldier you have, and every new one. Militia and Spearmen get iron weapons.

New buildings: Barracks, Archery Range, Blacksmith.

handbook.warbands.13.title: Commands
handbook.warbands.13.body:
Right-click: next order. Shift+right-click: back one.

Follow: an escort. They fight what attacks you or them, what you hit, and raiders near you. Ones 32+ blocks away come (not mid-fight, every 2 min).
Hold: guard the spot they're on.
Attack: hunt raiders, then monsters (not creepers), within 24 blocks, faster.

Tower archers stay posted. Goats drop horns ramming stone or logs.

Feudal: Forging (+1 damage), Fletching (range, aim), Scale Armor (+2 armor).
Castle: Blast Forging, Bodkin Arrows, Chain Mail (each builds on one above), Husbandry (knights).

handbook.warbands.raiders.title: Raiders
handbook.warbands.traps.title: Camp Traps
handbook.warbands.traps.body:
Camps are trapped — look before you step.

A brass plate rings a bell and the whole camp sallies out. A tripwire fires the dispensers beside it, or a powder keg: it hurts, but breaks nothing. Watch for open trapdoors over a fall, and for caltrops underfoot (Feudal age on).

Dispensers inside a camp can't be opened, and trap-shot arrows can't be picked up. Traps die with the camp: once it is claimed, they stop working.
handbook.warbands.contraptions.title: Camp Contraptions
handbook.warbands.contraptions.body:
Bigger camps run on redstone. Every trap is wired to a red War Relay that switches on when the alarm sounds: portcullises slam shut, guns fire once a second, rigged planks drop away.

Smash a relay and what it drives goes dead. They're the red blocks in the walls beside a gate, under a gun, at a plank's piston. Sculk sensors on a brass horn hear footsteps and mining: sneak past them, or muffle them with wool. A Ram breaks a portcullis.
handbook.warbands.threat.title: Threat
handbook.warbands.threat.body:
A camp's Threat (1-5 stars, on the War Map) sets how hard it hits.

Difficulty: Easy camps have fewer, weaker guards; Hard ones more, with more health and damage. Friends: every extra player near a camp when it's manned adds a guard and toughens the warlord. Streak: every two camps of an age you take adds a guard to the next.

Raids grow the same way with difficulty and the players at home.
handbook.warbands.raiders.body:
A rival warband: the same soldiers as yours, with a red headband and a white skull on the chest. Their battering ram has a black roof.

Your soldiers fight them on sight. They drop nothing and can't be claimed. Hit a camp and its guards throw the gates open and come after you. You meet them in their camps and when they raid your town.
handbook.warbands.war_map.title: War Maps
handbook.warbands.war_map.body:
Buy one with the map button at the Town Center. It's a real map: the red X is the camp, the blue banner your town. Hold it for the distance and an arrow.

Each age has several camp kinds (a keep, a cavalry encampment, a witch coven...), drawn in a shuffled order. Some only settle in their biome: forest, shore, swamp, snow...

Shift-click the map button to give up a camp.
handbook.warbands.taking_camps.title: Taking a Camp
handbook.warbands.taking_camps.body:
Kill every guard: a beam marks the banner. Right-click it for supplies for your town, a trophy and a War Chest.

Bandit and Fort trophies unlock the next age; Keep trophies are war prizes.

Then the camp burns and the map leads you home.
handbook.warbands.raids.title: Raids
handbook.warbands.raids.body:
When: from the Feudal Age, every few nights and the night after you take a camp, while you're near your town.

The warning names the kind: a mixed Warband, archer Night Stalkers (deep night only), a slow Shield Wall, and in Castle Age a Siege with rams or fast Cavalry. They break doors and buildings.

Defend the Town Center: unguarded, it loses a fifth of its stock.

Win for gold and their war chest (follow the smoke). Off on Peaceful.
handbook.warbands.repair.title: Repair
handbook.warbands.repair.body:
Raiders can't break core blocks, but a building below half its blocks stops working until repaired.

The anvil button at the Town Center rebuilds every building around it, block by block, for 1 stone per missing block. Not during a raid, and it never replaces your own blocks.

handbook.warbands.buildings.body:
Every building has a blueprint (recipe on its page) and needs your Town Center within 64 blocks. Its stone, and later its training, are paid from the Town Center.

Training queues share the town's population limit. Breaking a building refunds its queue.

New recipes appear in your recipe book when your town reaches their age.

handbook.warbands.warlords.title: Warlords
handbook.warbands.warlords.body:
Every Castle camp answers to a warlord, and its banner won't fall while he stands.

The Keep's warlord is a true boss with a red bar. As he weakens he rages: a war cry that whips up his guards, a charge, and a ground slam that throws you back.

The other Castle camps have lesser warlords: tough, but one-trick.
handbook.warbands.warlord_spoils.title: Warlord Spoils
handbook.warbands.warlord_spoils.body:
Each warlord drops a named weapon. The Keep's Vorak leaves his Brand and a piece of the Warlord's Plate; Brakk, Arha and Mos leave a lesser weapon of their own. Every warlord also drops a few emeralds, XP and an enchanted book.

Castle War Chests may also hold a piece of the Warlord's Plate.

A Cavalry Encampment may give a whistle that calls a tame, armored warhorse.

handbook.warbands.relics.title: Relics
handbook.warbands.relics.body:
The first win at each fantasy camp gives its relic. Craft a Relic Pedestal (blackstone, gold, an emerald), set it near your Town Center and put the relic on it: a gem lights up and the town gains an effect. One of each:
- Hag's Charm: soldiers heal.
- Frost Sigil: raids call out sooner.
- Grave Lantern: the dead sap foes.
- Omen Banner: faster horses.
handbook.warbands.relics.witch_coven.eff: The Hag's Charm: your soldiers slowly knit their wounds.
The Frost Sigil: raids on this town call out sooner.

handbook.warbands.relics.illager_hall.ef: The Omen Banner: your horses run faster in town.

handbook.warbands.caches.title: Caches and props
handbook.warbands.caches.body:
Each camp hides one or two stash chests, the ones nearest the banner. Whoever opens one first takes its loot, so share. They burn with the camp: open them before you claim the standard. Breaking one spills its loot but never drops the chest.

Camps show what they do. Hunters hang hides, forts and keeps line up weapon racks, smugglers pile crates, and each kind's raiders wear their own colors. You can craft the props to dress your own town.
camp_layout.warbands.bandit_camp: A bandit hideout: the chief's red tent at the back, archers on steps by the gate. The west wall has fallen in, but a berry pit waits just inside the gap.
camp_layout.warbands.poachers_lodge: A hunters' lodge behind a palisade: mostly archers, one on a high seat. A snare string by the cookfire fires an arrow trap in the wall.
camp_layout.warbands.smugglers_dock: An open landing with no wall at all; archers on the jetty. Once the alarm sounds, the loose plank on the jetty drops you into the water.
camp_layout.warbands.fort: A square stone fort with two gate towers. Tripwire and caltrops at the gate.
camp_layout.warbands.quarry_stronghold: Cobblestone walls round a quarry pit; crossbows on the towers.
camp_layout.warbands.witch_coven: A hut on stilts over a lily pond, inside a hedge of mangrove roots. Two witches throw potions from the porch, and a berry pit waits at the foot of the stair: bring milk.
camp_layout.warbands.frozen_outpost: A trappers' outpost behind a snow wall: a longhouse, an igloo, an archer on the watchtower. Powder snow under the open trapdoors on the path.
camp_layout.warbands.keep: High walls and a reinforced gate only a Battering Ram breaks.
camp_layout.warbands.cavalry_encampment: An open paddock full of knights. Spears and a narrow spot help.
camp_layout.warbands.sunken_crypt: A vault dug into the ground: one stair down, and a powder keg at its foot.
camp_layout.warbands.illager_hall: A raiders' hall in a dark-oak ring. Kegs wired at the hall door.
camp_layout.warbands.bandit_stockade: A round log fort. A roofed lookout over the gate holds an archer; berry pits flank the path in. The standard stands before the longhouse at the back.
camp_layout.warbands.poachers_treehouse: Four treehouse platforms with archers, joined by rope bridges whose middle planks drop away when the alarm sounds. Ladders up each trunk; sculk sensors listen in the yard.
camp_layout.warbands.smugglers_warehouse: Two warehouses and a dark alley to a counting house. Sculk sensors in the alley: sneak. Two guns in the counting house wall cover the alley; the red relays under them silence them.
camp_layout.warbands.fort_barbican: The gate opens into a walled barbican: two guns a side and a portcullis that drops when the alarm sounds. Smash the red relays in its walls, or climb through the breach in the west wall, past two sculk sensors (sneak).
camp_layout.warbands.fort_twin: Two wards. A cross wall with four guns and a portcullis guards the inner one. Side gates in both wards open when the alarm sounds: lead your troops around the wall through them. A small north postern leads into the inner ward, past sculk sensors.
camp_layout.warbands.quarry_terraces: A stepped quarry hill: two terraces, switchback ramps, guns in the retaining walls and a keg wire on the upper walkway. Crossbows up top, so keep low and keep moving.
camp_layout.warbands.quarry_minehead: A mine head: a tall headframe in the middle with crossbows on top and four guns at its foot, and a powder magazine north-west that goes up if its tripwire is crossed.
camp_layout.warbands.coven_stilts: Huts on stilts over a bog, joined by plank walkways that drop away when the alarm sounds. Guns with Slowness arrows face the stairs. Three witches: bring milk.
camp_layout.warbands.coven_grove: A stone circle inside an azalea hedge. The four standing stones at the compass points hide potion throwers aimed at the altar; smash the red stone at their feet. Sculk sensors listen at the hedge.
camp_layout.warbands.frozen_starfort: A star fort of ice: archers under the spires of three bastions, a great igloo keep in the middle. Powder snow under the open trapdoors on the path, two guns on spruce posts, sculk sensors in the side points.
camp_layout.warbands.frozen_glacier: A glacier with a cavern inside: one tunnel, sealed by a portcullis when the alarm sounds. Its relays are buried in the ice beside the gate, and ice digs fast: dig your own way in. Sculk sensors inside hear mining, so sneak while you dig.
camp_layout.warbands.keep_moat: An island castle: a moat all round, one causeway to a gate only a Ram breaks, guns in the gatehouse. The inner keep drops a portcullis when the alarm sounds. A postern at the back is only reached by swimming, and sculk sensors listen behind it.
camp_layout.warbands.keep_concentric: A concentric castle: an outer wall, then a corridor of traps round an inner wall whose portcullis gate is on the far (north) side. Guns in the inner wall sweep the corridor; each has its red relay under it. The warlord holds the central keep.
camp_layout.warbands.cavalry_ring: A round horse arena: six knights ride the track, crossbows on two platforms, caltrops at the gate and two guns at the pavilion. Spears and a narrow gate stop a charge.
camp_layout.warbands.cavalry_paddocks: Two paddocks of knights either side of a long fenced run lined with guns; their relays are the red blocks at the foot of each post. Or break through a paddock fence and fight the knights first.
camp_layout.warbands.crypt_catacomb: A catacomb under the ground: a maze of dark corridors with sculk sensors in some rooms and the dead in others. The tomb in the middle drops a portcullis; its relays sit in the tomb wall beside the gate.
camp_layout.warbands.crypt_flooded: A flooded crypt sunk into the ground: islands joined by planks, one of which drops away when the alarm sounds; drowned in the channels and guns in the pillars.
camp_layout.warbands.illager_watchtower: A raiders' hall and a tall watchtower joined by a rope bridge; pillagers shoot from the tower top and the hall roof. A bridge plank drops when the alarm sounds. Climb the tower from inside.
camp_layout.warbands.illager_longhouse: A long illager manor: rooms of vindicators either side of a central hall, guns in its walls, and a portcullis before the throne room. The rooms have windows: you can break in from the side.
